worksheet.title: Fix the Order
worksheet.subtitle: Find the wrong step and fix it
worksheet.learning_goal: I can find the step that is wrong and fix it so Bit reaches the star.

parts.title: Bit's steps did not work
parts.text: Bit followed the arrows but did NOT reach the star. One step is wrong, or one is missing or extra. Finding and fixing it is called DEBUGGING. Bit starts on box 1; the star is on box 3.

parts.title: Watch Bit — these steps land on box 2, not the star
parts.note: ➡ ⬅ ➡ goes right, left, right — Bit ends on box 2. The ⬅ is the wrong step. Fix: ➡ ➡.

parts.title: A step is missing
parts.prompt: The star is on box 4. Bit's steps ➡ ➡ only reach box 3. What is missing? Draw the fix (the whole correct program).

parts.title: A step is extra
parts.prompt: The star is on box 2. Bit's steps ➡ ➡ go too far to box 3. Cross out the extra arrow and draw the fix.

parts.title: You try — a wrong turn
parts.prompt: The star is on box 3. Bit's steps ⬅ ➡ ➡ land on box 2. Circle the wrong arrow and draw the fix.

parts.title: Big idea
parts.text: When a plan does not work, you find the wrong step and fix it — that is debugging. Every coder does it, and so can you!

parts.title: What this worksheet teaches
parts.text: Children test a set of arrows, find the step that is wrong, missing, or extra, and fix it so Bit reaches the star. Testing and fixing a plan is debugging — the K-friendly close to sequencing. No coding experience needed.

parts.title: Before you start (no computer needed)
parts.text: No computer — paper and a pencil or crayon. You read each prompt aloud. Optional: tape a row of numbered boxes (and a star) on the floor so a child can walk the steps.

parts.title: How to lead it (about 15 minutes)
text: 1. Show them (you do). Run a plan that misses the star: "it lands on the wrong box — let's find the problem and fix it."
2. Do one together. Exercise 1 — the plan is one step short; add one more right arrow.
3. Let them try. Children fix Exercise 2 (remove an extra arrow) and Exercise 3 (replace a wrong arrow).

parts.title: Answer key (these are the verified correct answers)
text: Exercise 1 — two right arrows reach only box 3; a step is missing; fix to three right arrows (box 4).

Exercise 2 — two right arrows overshoot to box 3; remove one arrow; fix to one right arrow (box 2). Exercise 3 — left, right, right lands on box 2; the first arrow (left) is wrong; fix to two right arrows (box 3).

parts.title: If children get stuck — and ways to adjust
text: Watch for: rewriting the whole plan instead of finding the one problem. Run the plan and watch where it goes wrong.
Make it easier: walk the buggy plan on the floor boxes to feel the miss.
Make it harder: have the child make a buggy plan for a partner to find and fix.
Make it active: step out the buggy plan, then step out the fix.

parts.title: Ontario Kindergarten link (official wording)
text: Problem Solving and Innovating — children detect and correct an error in a sequence of steps.
In plain terms: testing a plan, finding the wrong, missing, or extra step, and fixing it — a first taste of debugging.
No reading is needed from the child — you read each prompt aloud; the child answers by circling, numbering, or drawing arrows.

parts.title: You'll know it worked when
parts.text: The child finds the wrong, missing, or extra arrow and fixes the plan so Bit reaches the star.
